---
title: "AI for Agriculturists & Biologists"
subtitle: "A two-day, hands-on workshop — from first principles to honest models, with every lab in Python and R"
toc: false
---

This workshop takes agricultural and biological researchers from "what is AI?" to training, testing and critically judging machine-learning models on their own kind of data. No programming experience is required: every lab runs in the browser through Google Colab, and every lab comes in both **Python** and **R**.

The examples come from the work participants do: field trials and yield, plant disease, genomic prediction and **population genetics**, soil **metagenomics**, transcriptomics, leaf images and protein sequences.

## What you will be able to do

1. Explain the difference between AI, machine learning, deep learning and large language models, with examples from biology and agriculture.
2. Prepare biological data for machine learning: missing values, outliers, genotype QC, compositional microbiome counts.
3. Train, evaluate and interpret classification and regression models.
4. Spot the pitfalls that make models look better than they are: data leakage, relatives and population structure, site and batch effects.
5. Use pre-trained models — image networks, AlphaFold, protein language models — without training from scratch.
6. Use LLM assistants responsibly, and verify what they produce.
7. Plan an AI project for a question from your own research.

## How to use this site

- **Participants:** start with [Setup](setup.qmd). Each module page has short notes followed by the lab. Switch between **Python** and **R** with the tabs; your choice is remembered across pages. Use the **Open in Colab** buttons to run a lab yourself.
- **Instructors:** see the [Schedule](schedule.qmd) and the [Instructor notes](instructors.qmd) for timing, teaching tips and how to rebuild the labs.

All datasets are simulated to look like real data — including the real problems — so they can be shared freely and every lesson works as intended. See [Datasets](resources/datasets.qmd).
